research_concepts: shot mix (shot distance and zone distribution)
substitution rotation intervals and reconstructed lineups
methodological_questions: Does a pre-specified change in the offensive five shift shot mix by more than a null swap does?
Is the shift larger than what the incoming and outgoing players' own shot profiles would mechanically predict?
How should opponent lineup, score, clock, period and fatigue be handled in a stint-based comparison?
Is exposure per swap type sufficient at team-stint level?
Can shot mix be measured from shot distance and zone fields without relying on noisy play-type labels?

historical_evidence.finding: Opponent lineup adaptation, with the opposing rim big off the floor. On N=1.07M possessions: DRIVE +0.82pp (SE 0.25), POST_UP +0.43pp (SE 0.18), 3PA -1.79pp (SE 0.31), rim <=4ft +0.12pp (t=+0.4), PPP +0.008 (t=+1.1). The record says the sub-1pp mix shifts are WEAK/SMALL. Limited by small sample; risk SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER. This is a defensive-personnel manipulation, not a change in the offensive five.
Descriptive within-game play-type mix shifts (halftime, crunch, post-run). No inferential tests. The OTHER label is recorded as noisy. Risks LABEL_ERROR and MEASURE_RELIABILITY.

After-timeout possessions show large play-type mix shifts (POST_UP +2.406, t=+18.7; SPOT_UP +2.333) against a same game-offense-period-minute comparison. Descriptive. It uses the reconstructed-lineups dataset.

The PULL_UP exposure effect shrank from -0.0255 with lineup fixed effects to -0.0063 without them. The same-shooter placebo on other play types was about -0.0075, consistent with a shooter-level confound. Risks CONFOUNDING and PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE.
The claimed connector lineup ORtg lift was recorded as a talent confound (p=0.51 after TALENT control). Risks CONFOUNDING and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.
Lineup-specific suppression cells (n>=30) were reported with no placebo or matching. The record says later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts. Risk PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE.
The matchup decomposition used cells of n=15-54 and was limited by insufficient exposure. Risk EXPOSURE_SPARSITY.
Defensive scheme labels reached only 14.9% and 3.3% usable rates, and switches_on was not populated. Failed gate (A_unanswerable).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Interpreting a lineup-conditioned slope as a causal effect without a placebo
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact: the effect shrank without lineup fixed effects and the same-shooter placebo was of similar size, consistent with a shooter-level confound.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading lineup-cell differences with no placebo or matching
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as having no placebo or matching; similar gaps were later treated as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing lineup lift to a presence variable without controlling for talent

failed_approaches.why: Recorded as insufficient exposure, with cell n of 15-54 (EXPOSURE_SPARSITY).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball coverage from matchup and PBP fields
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as a label-rate failure (A_unanswerable) with low coverage.
The OTHER label is recorded as noisy (LABEL_ERROR).

evidence_establishes: FAM:SF34 shows that a mix shift from an opponent-personnel manipulation is detectable at N=1.07M possessions: SEs were about 0.25-0.31pp for DRIVE and 3PA share, and 3PA moved -1.79pp (t=-5.8). Its status is recorded as inconclusive, though, because other outcomes were weak or small.
The recorded history repeatedly shows lineup- or player-conditioned differences being confounded by player identity or talent (FAM:SF-TMP-009, FAM:SF-APPS-087, FAM:SF-CHT-009).
Play-type labels, including OTHER, are recorded as noisy, and tactical labels derived from matchup feeds had low coverage (FAM:SF-APPM-021, FAM:SF-APPS-058).
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests whether changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, so the stated positive control has not been run.
The records give no estimate of the size of shot-mix shifts per single-player swap, and no sample-size or exposure requirement for five-man units.
They do not show whether a swap shift exceeds what the swapped players' own shot profiles mechanically predict.
They do not show that shot-distance-based mix is more reliable than play-type labels. This is only suggested.
own_inferences: As worded, the claim is close to tautological: players differ in shot profiles, so swapping a rim-running big for a perimeter wing must shift shot distance mix. A pass would show only that the pipeline recovers a mechanically expected effect, not a causal lineup effect.

The control is informative as a sensitivity check only if it is stated quantitatively: the observed shift should track the shift predicted from the swapped players' out-of-sample profiles, and matched-profile swaps should show about zero.
Shot distance and zone from PBP should be the outcome, rather than play-type labels, because of the recorded label noise.

Substitutions are endogenous (fatigue, foul trouble, score, garbage time, opponent lineup), so raw before/after comparisons are confounded. Within-game adjacent-stint comparisons with covariates and placebo swaps are needed.
Single-player swaps will probably be far more common than whole-five changes, so the design should define 'changing the five' as the swap of k>=1 players and stratify by swap type.
The sample is large enough (about 3 seasons, thousands of team-stints per swap type for common swaps), but rare five-man units will be sparse.
uncertainties: The true per-possession SD of shot-mix indicators within stints is unknown here, so the minimum detectable effect is not computed.
Lineup reconstruction accuracy from rotation intervals, and the handling of mid-possession substitutions, are not verified.
Whether the PBP shot-distance fields are consistent across the 2022-23 to 2024-25 seasons is unknown.
Assignment of possessions to lineups at stint boundaries may be noisy.
No record shows how often the project's pipeline has recovered known effects.

historical_effect.explanation: No record tests the question, so history does not tell us the answer. It changed the design and the decision: from a plain 'proceed' to proceed_with_changes. The artifact and confound records (FAM:SF-TMP-009, FAM:SF-APPS-087, FAM:SF-CHT-009) call for placebo and matched-swap controls and for a player-profile-adjusted estimand. The label-noise records (FAM:SF-APPM-021, FAM:SF-APPS-058) call for shot-distance outcomes. The sub-1pp, SE about 0.25-0.3pp result in FAM:SF34 calls for pre-specified effect-size thresholds, so a detectable but trivial shift does not count as validation.

blocking_constraints.text: Substitution timing and player identity are confounded with fatigue, score, foul trouble and the opposing lineup. Without profile-adjusted and placebo-swap comparisons, a pass cannot be distinguished from mechanical player-profile composition.
Full-five changes and rare swap types will have little exposure. Primary inference must be limited to common single-swap classes.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests an offensive-five change against shot mix. FAM:SF34 (inconclusive) is the nearest, for opponent personnel, and shows detectable but small mix shifts. Other records contribute only methodological cautions on confounding, placebo use and label noise.

risks.text: Substitution decisions depend on game state, fatigue and fouls. Opponent lineup and score margin also shift shot mix. Adjacent-stint comparison within game with covariates is needed.
The shift must beat matched-profile and permuted swaps. A raw nonzero shift is not evidence of design sensitivity.
If the profile prediction is built from the same games as the test, 'expected' shifts are partly outcome-derived. Profiles must be estimated out of sample.
Player shot profiles must be built from other games (leave-game-out or prior-season/prior-games only), not from the same stint.
Play-type labels (OTHER) are noisy. Primary outcomes should be shot distance and zone from PBP.
Lineup reconstruction from rotation intervals can misassign possessions around substitutions. Validate against PBP substitution events and exclude boundary possessions.
Rare swap types give wide intervals. Restrict to swap classes with a pre-set minimum number of stint pairs.
Several mix outcomes and swap classes. Use a pre-specified primary family with Holm correction.
Shot mix trends across seasons and playoffs vs. regular season. Include season and stage fixed effects.

design.estimand: For team-stint pairs that differ by a single-player swap (outgoing A, incoming B) of a pre-defined swap class, the within-game difference in shot mix (rim share <=4ft, three-point attempt share, mid-range share, mean shot distance) in the post-swap vs pre-swap stint, and the ratio of that difference to the shift predicted from A's and B's out-of-sample shot profiles. Positive control passes if the shift is in the predicted direction, a pre-set share of the predicted magnitude, and clearly larger than for matched-profile and permuted swaps.
design.unit: Team offensive stint pair (adjacent stints in the same game and period segment, with lineup change by exactly one player) with possession-level shot outcomes inside each stint; clustered by game.
design.sample: All regular-season and playoff games 2022-23 to 2024-25. Include half-court and transition possessions that produce a field-goal attempt. Exclude garbage time (pre-defined margin and clock rule), stints under a minimum number of possessions, possessions at substitution boundaries, and ejections or injury-forced sequences, which are flagged for sensitivity analysis. Lineups are reconstructed from rotation intervals and validated against PBP substitution events.
design.power: Before looking at outcomes, estimate within-stint variance of each outcome from a held-out season (or random game subset), then compute the minimum detectable effect for each swap class given its stint-pair count. Only classes with at least a pre-registered number of stint pairs are used for the primary test, and the MDE for each class is reported. For context, FAM:SF34 reached SE of about 0.25-0.31pp on N=1.07M possessions; per-class SEs here will be larger. A swap class where the MDE exceeds half the predicted shift is reported as underpowered, not as a failure.
design.controls: Player shot profiles (zone distribution) estimated out of sample (other games or prior seasons) with shrinkage; covariates for score margin, period, clock, opponent five (or opponent big presence), home/away, stage (regular season vs playoffs) and season; game fixed effects through the within-game design. Negative control: swaps between matched-profile players (nearest neighbours on profile and position) should yield about zero shift. Placebo: randomly relabelled swap times within the same game and permuted swap-class labels.
design.falsification: The control fails if (a) matched-profile swaps show shifts comparable to those for contrasting swaps, (b) the shift does not track the profile-predicted shift (slope not clearly positive), or (c) the permuted-time placebo gives similar shifts. A failure is reported as a design sensitivity problem rather than a result about lineups.
design.multiplicity: Primary family: rim share, three-point share, mid-range share, with one contrasting swap class (a rim-running big replaced by a non-big wing or guard) and one slope test of observed vs predicted shifts. Holm correction at alpha=0.05 over the primary family. Other swap classes and outcomes are exploratory and labelled as such.
design.decision_rule: Declare the positive control passed if all of the following hold: the contrasting-swap shift in rim share is in the predicted direction with Holm-adjusted p<0.05; its magnitude is at least a pre-set fraction (for example 50%) of the profile-predicted shift; the matched-swap shift has a CI that excludes the contrasting-swap shift; and the placebo gives a null result. If the shift is significant but below the pre-set practical threshold (for example under 1pp, as in FAM:SF34), report it as detectable but small. If the placebos show comparable shifts, report as artifact. If the MDE is too large, report as underpowered.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play, substitution rotation intervals, starters and box-score summary for 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, as available on 2026-11-02. Freeze the data snapshot and lineup reconstruction code (version-tagged) before any analysis, use shot distance and result fields from PBP for outcomes, and do not use graph play-type labels as primary outcomes.

research_concepts: shot mix (shot distance and zone distribution)
design sensitivity / positive-control detection of personnel effects
substitution rotation intervals and five-man units
methodological_questions: Does changing one or more players in the offensive five shift shot mix measurably?
Can the design detect known personnel effects (positive control) with the available per-game play-by-play data?
How should confounding from opponent, game state, score, and clock be handled when comparing lineups?
What sample size and exposure per lineup are needed given sparse five-man possessions?
How to avoid player-identity versus lineup-composition confounding and selection of substitutions?
args.query: Prior studies on whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix (shot distance/zone distribution), used as a positive-control showing the design can detect personnel effects, using play-by-play and rotation data from NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-02, in the area of lineup and matchup effects):
Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm settling on the final answer now, without more tool calls. The offensive five is a natural positive control: swapping personnel shifts shot mix by construction, since players carry different shot profiles. The concern is that this is tautological, so I'd want to define the swap more carefully, such as replacing a rim-running big with a perimeter shooter, so the check is meaningful.

I'm sketching the design now: units are team-possession stints around single-player swaps, with the shot-mix change predicted from each player's out-of-sample season profile. The positive control swaps a rim-running big for a perimeter player, a negative control swaps players with matched profiles, and a placebo permutes the swap labels, all while accounting for fatigue, score, clock, and opponent lineup.

I'm planning the statistics now: the design reports a shot-mix change per unit with a standard error in the range of a quarter point, and the single-player effect is expected to be several points, so the power is probably adequate. I'm also settling on three primary outcomes with a multiplicity correction, and the data will be frozen over the 2022-23 to 2024-25 play-by-play, with lineups rebuilt from substitution intervals. Shot zones from distance, not play-type labels, since those are noisy, and the decision rule gets pre-specified before I write it up.
